TIME_SPEED_HINT: Speed {speed}: {days} days per second (keys 1–5, or + and − on the number pad)

COUNTRY_SELECTION_HINT: Click a country on the map, search for one, or pick one below.

COUNTRY_SCREEN_INTEREST_GROUPS_HINT: Each group's clout as a slice of the pie, with its approval of the government.
COUNTRY_SCREEN_NATIONAL_MODIFIERS_NONE: None yet. They arrive with the systems that put lasting effects on a country.
COUNTRY_SCREEN_LAWS_HINT: Click a law to open the Laws screen.

TOP_BAR_POLITICAL_CAPITAL_HINT: Spent on laws and reforms. Opens the government screen.
TOP_BAR_INFLUENCE_HINT: Spent to sway public opinion. Opens public opinion.
TOP_BAR_LEGITIMACY_HINT: How accepted the government is. Opens the government screen.
TOP_BAR_STABILITY_HINT: How calm the country is. Opens population and pops.
TOP_BAR_MANPOWER_HINT: People available to serve in the army. Opens armies and fronts.
TOP_BAR_PILOTS_HINT: Trained pilots ready for mechs and aircraft. Opens the unit roster.
TOP_BAR_FOOD_HINT: Food reserves in days of what your country eats and uses. Opens the Food screen.
TOP_BAR_SWARM_CONTROL_HINT: How much of the world the Swarm holds. Opens Swarm intel.
TOP_BAR_ARRIVAL_HINT: Time left until Object Alpha arrives (Phase 0). Opens the journal.
ALERT_HINT: Click to go there · right-click to dismiss
ALERT_LAYOFFS_TEXT: {jobs} jobs closed. {building} in {province} loses money even at its lowest wage and keeps {open} of its jobs open.
ALERT_SHORTAGE_TITLE: Shortages: your people went without {share} of their goods
ALERT_SHORTAGE_TEXT: Most short: {good} (people got {got} of what they wanted today). The Markets screen shows every good.
SCREEN_EMPTY: This screen is empty for now. It fills in when its feature is built.
POPULATION_DEPENDENTS_HINT: Children, the elderly and others who don't work. They need food and goods, but have no job.
POPULATION_STANDARD_OF_LIVING_HINT: From 1 to 99: people's wealth, what their income buys at their market's prices (as in Victoria 3). It climbs slowly while their income pays for more, falls while it doesn't, and shortages of the goods they buy lower it.
POPULATION_INCOME_HINT: What one worker earned last week, as a year's income in US dollars: wages and, for owners, the dividends of the province's buildings. It also feeds the worker's dependents.
POPULATION_PLACEHOLDER_NOTE: Jobs come from buildings and, for the rest of the economy, from a stand-in that keeps pace with the workforce and pays wages from each country's real GDP. People buy goods on their country's market; housing, services and luxuries have no good yet and cost what local work costs.
BUILDINGS_OUTPUT_HINT: How much of its full output a building makes today. Missing workers, electricity or inputs lower it.
BUILDINGS_METHOD_HINT: How the building works. Poorer countries mostly run labor-intensive methods (many workers, few machines). Switching methods comes with F88.
BUILDINGS_RECIPE_HINT: At full output, level {level}: makes {makes} a day; uses {uses} a day; {jobs} workers.
BUILDINGS_LIMIT_DEMAND: No more electricity is needed today.
BUILDINGS_TEST_NOTE: Change levels by hand to try things out. Real construction comes with F12 (M3).
BUILDINGS_SCREEN_TYPES_HINT: Click a building to see where it stands.
BUILDINGS_SCREEN_NONE: {country} has no buildings. Its people work in the rest of the economy.
BUILDINGS_PLACEHOLDER_NOTE: Every country starts with its real buildings (2024 production figures; approximate). Buildings offer about a third of the world's jobs: farming and the industries in the catalog. The rest (services, construction, vehicles and machinery) is still the rest of the economy. Prices and profits come with F65, trade with F19, construction with F12.
STOCKPILE_HINT: What your buildings make goes into the national stockpile; what they use comes out of it. It keeps at most {days} days' worth; the rest is lost.
STOCKPILE_IMPORTED_HINT: What arrives from abroad every morning (trade: see the Trade screen).
STOCKPILE_OTHER_ELECTRICITY: Rest of the economy and homes
STOCKPILE_OTHER_ELECTRICITY_HINT: Homes, shops and offices use most of a country's electricity. It grows with the population; when the power plants can't keep up, everyone gets less.
STOCKPILE_TEST_FILL_HINT: Tops the stockpile up to {days} days of what your buildings use, like emergency imports. A test tool: trade comes with F19 (M4).
PANEL_BACK_HINT: Back to the panel you came from
SETTINGS_HINT: Message settings, alerts, and facts about this build
SETTINGS_MESSAGES_HINT: Choose how each kind of message is shown. Your browser remembers these settings.
SETTINGS_MESSAGES_MORE: More kinds of message arrive with the features that cause them (events, news, wars…).
SETTINGS_ALERTS_HINT: Turn off the alerts you don't want in the alerts row under the top bar. Your browser remembers these settings.
SETTINGS_ABOUT_HINT: Technical facts about this version of the game, useful in bug reports.
CREDITS_MAP: Borders, coasts and rivers: made with Natural Earth (public domain).
CREDITS_ELEVATION: Terrain heights: Terrain Tiles (Mapzen, hosted as Amazon open data). GMTED2010 terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; ETOPO1 terrain data by the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
CREDITS_LAND_COVER: Land cover: © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by the ESA WorldCover consortium. Licensed under CC BY 4.0; reduced to the game's terrain tiles.
CREDITS_STATISTICS: Starting population and economy: World Bank (World Development Indicators) and International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook).
CREDITS_POPULATION: Where people live: Kontur Population, Global Population Density for 400m H3 Hexagons, © Kontur. Licensed under CC BY 4.0; reduced to the people counted in each province.
CREDITS_PRODUCTION: Starting buildings: energy production and electricity by source from Our World in Data's energy dataset (Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy; Ember), licensed under CC BY 4.0; farm, fishery and industry figures from the World Bank; steel, iron ore, copper, bauxite, aluminum and silicon approximately from worldsteel and the U.S. Geological Survey.
CREDITS_MARKETS: Markets: base prices are approximate 2024 world prices (World Bank commodity price data), typed in by hand; the market and pop rules are modelled on Paradox Interactive's Victoria 3 (as described on its community wiki and in Paradox's developer diaries).
MESSAGE_LOG_HINT: Every message so far, newest first
DEMO_OWNER_CHANGE: Hand a province to a neighbor
DEMO_OWNER_CHANGE_HINT: Gives a random border province to the neighboring country, which sends a real "province changed hands" message
DEMO_ALERT_TEXT: [Sample] A made-up alert for trying the alerts row.
DEMO_TOAST_TEXT: Small messages appear here and fade after a few seconds. Click one to go to its place.
DEMO_POPUP_TEXT: Important messages open a window like this one. Each message type can be set to pop up, show as a toast, go to the log only, or be off.
STRESS_LOADING: Putting the late-game load on the map…
STRESS_LOAD: On the map: {buildings} buildings, {units} units, {bugs} bugs in a battle, {lines} infrastructure lines, {particles} rain, smoke and fire particles, {clouds} clouds, laser beams
STRESS_BUDGETS: Goals: {strategic} FPS with the whole world in view, {close} FPS up close and at the battle.
STRESS_COPIED: Copied: paste them in the chat
STRESS_PART_HINT: Show or hide this part of the load, to see what it costs
POPULATION_NEED_NO_GOOD: no good yet: paid at local prices
MARKETS_PRICE_HINT: This week's price on your country's market, in US dollars per tonne (per megawatt-hour for electricity).
MARKETS_VS_BASE_HINT: The price as a share of the good's base price (its real-world price in 2024): ×1.00 is the base price; shortages push it up to ×1.75, surpluses down to ×0.25.
MARKETS_HISTORY_HINT: The price week by week since the game started or was loaded (up to a year). The dashed line is the base price.
MARKETS_HISTORY_WEEKS: The price over the last {weeks} weeks
MARKETS_SELL_HINT: Sell orders: what your country's buildings make in a day, plus what arrives from abroad (marked *). For electricity: what the power plants could make.
MARKETS_BUY_HINT: Buy orders: what everyone wants to buy in a day. More buy orders than sell orders raise the price next week.
MARKETS_POPS_GOT: People got {share} of what they wanted today.
MARKETS_REST_HINT: The rest of the economy: everything the buildings in the game don't cover yet (construction, vehicles, machinery…). It buys less of what gets dearer, at home or abroad.
MARKETS_SHORTAGE: Last week your people went without {share} of the goods they wanted.
MARKETS_NO_SHORTAGE: Last week your people got all the goods they wanted.
MARKETS_HINT: Every Monday each price moves with last week's buy and sell orders (Victoria 3's rule): price = reference price × (1 + 0.75 × (buy − sell) ÷ the smaller of the two), between ×0.25 and ×1.75 of the base price. The reference price is the base price, or for a good your country imports, the average of its own goods and the imports' delivered cost (world price + shipping + tariff). The stock is a reserve: buyers draw on it, prices ignore it.
MARKETS_NOTE: Imports are sold here like your own goods; exporters buy here like everyone else, after your own buyers. See the Trade screen for who you trade with.
BUILDINGS_PROFIT_HINT: What the buildings sell today, less their inputs and electricity at market prices and their wages (US dollars). Part of a profit goes into the building's cash reserves, the rest to the province's owners as dividends.
BUILDINGS_WAGE_LEVEL_HINT: What the buildings pay as a multiple of the going local wage (as in Victoria 3): they raise it when they make a good profit but can't fill their jobs, and cut it when they lose money.
BUILDINGS_LAYING_OFF_HINT: Buildings that lose money even at their lowest wage close part of their jobs, a tenth a week; they hire back once they make money again.
BUILDINGS_SUBSISTENCE_WAGES: {amount} a day: its workers share what it makes
MARKETS_SELL_IMPORTED: Of this, {amount} a day arrived from abroad.
MARKETS_EXPORTS_HINT: What your exporters buy in a day to sell abroad. They get what is left after your own buyers.
TRADE_BALANCE_HINT: Exports less imports, a day. The money goes into the treasury once there is one (F09).
TRADE_TARIFFS_HINT: What your tariffs bring in a day (a share of each imported good's base price). Into the treasury with F09.
TRADE_FROM_REST: From the rest of the world
TRADE_REST_OF_WORLD_HINT: A stand-in: it sells what the world's buildings can't make enough of yet (electronics, fuel, iron ore, copper ore), more as the world's population grows.
TRADE_HINT: Every country trades on one World Market (Victoria 3). Each Monday your traders import more of what your market lacks and export more of what it has spare; imports cost the world price plus shipping and your {tariff} tariff. Goods move every day: exports leave your stockpile, imports arrive the next morning.
TRADE_HOME_PRICE_HINT: This week's price on your country's market.
TRADE_WORLD_PRICE_HINT: The World Market's price: it follows what the whole world wants and makes, between ×0.25 and ×1.75 of the base price.
TRADE_DELIVERED_HINT: What a unit of your imports costs when it arrives: world price + shipping + tariff (and how much that adds to the world price).
TRADE_SELF_HINT: What your country makes as a share of what it uses itself. Under 100 %: it needs imports.
TRADE_ARRIVED: Only {share} of what the world's importers planned arrived today: exporters couldn't ship it all.
TRADE_ROUTE_HINT: The cheapest route between the two capitals over land and sea, and what shipping a tonne costs on it ($20 per 1,000 km by land, $1.50 by sea).
TRADE_TEST_HINT: Until diplomacy (M6): stop or restart trade with a country. Your importers turn to other suppliers at once.
TRADE_WORLD_HINT: The world price of every good that can be shipped (electricity can't, until the power grid, F74), what the world trades a day, and who exports and imports most.
TRADE_NOTE: Not yet: trade agreements, embargoes and sanctions made through diplomacy and the UN (M6), trade-policy laws that set tariffs, ports and fleets that limit how much a country can ship (F86), and routes cut by the Swarm.
ALERT_FAMINE_TEXT: Worst: {province}, where {starving} of the people starve. {deaths} people have died of hunger so far. Ration food, import more or win back farmland (the Food screen shows everything).
ALERT_FOOD_LOW_TEXT: Last week {shortage} of your people's basic food was missing. Rationing: {rationing}. The Food screen shows where your food comes from.
MESSAGE_FAMINE_STARTED: Famine has broken out in {province}: more than a third of its people are starving. People will die and fewer children will be born until food comes back.
MESSAGE_FAMINE_ENDED: The famine in {province} is over. It killed {deaths} people.
FOOD_HINT: Food is grain (all crops), livestock and fish, and processed food. People buy basic food and better food as part of their needs; ranches and food factories use grain too. How well people are fed follows Victoria 3: food security falls with the share of their income they spend on basic food and with the share of basic food that is missing.
FOOD_RESERVES_HINT: The food in your national stockpile, in days of what your country buys of it today. A campaign starts with 30 days; trade tops them up toward 30 days; at most 90 days are kept.
FOOD_SHORTAGE_HINT: The share of the basic food your people wanted last week that they didn't get.
FOOD_SECURITY_HINT: How well people are fed (Victoria 3): 100 % less the share of their income spent on basic food, less 1.5 × the share of basic food missing. It moves half the way there each week. Below 40 % people starve, below 20 % they starve severely.
FOOD_STARVING_HINT: People below 40 % food security: fewer births, more deaths, a lower standard of living. Below 20 % (severe) many die.
FOOD_FAMINE_HINT: A province is in famine while at least 35 % of its people starve and 15 % starve severely (Victoria 3).
FOOD_RATIONING_AUTOMATIC_HINT: Your country rations by itself as its food reserves fall (below 15 days light, 7 strict, 3 emergency) or food runs short, and eases off one level a week once they recover.
FOOD_RATIONING_LIGHT_HINT: The rest of the economy gets 25 % less food, people buy 20 % less better food. Costs 1 point of standard of living.
FOOD_RATIONING_STRICT_HINT: The rest of the economy gets half its food, people buy half their better food, and no food is exported. Costs 3 points of standard of living.
FOOD_RATIONING_EMERGENCY_HINT: The rest of the economy gets a tenth of its food, people get only basic food, and no food is exported. Costs 6 points of standard of living.
FOOD_PEOPLE_HINT: What your people bought today (red: they got less than they wanted).
FOOD_BUILDINGS_HINT: Ranches feed grain to livestock; food processing plants turn grain and livestock into processed food.
FOOD_GROUPS_TITLE: How each pop group is fed
FOOD_NOBODY_HUNGRY: Nobody in your country is starving.
FOOD_NOTE: Not yet: the Rationing law with its political cost (F16), stability, unrest and riots from hunger (F10), famine events (F95), seasons and harvests (F54), refugees who need feeding (F33), and the Swarm taking farmland (M7).
FOOD_TEST_CRISIS_HINT: Closes every farm, ranch, fishery and food factory in your country, empties its food reserves and stops all trade with it, so you can watch hunger, rationing and famine come. Reload the page to start over.
TOP_BAR_TREASURY_DEBT: Debt {debt} ({share} of GDP); {used} of the credit limit used; rating {rating}
TOP_BAR_TREASURY_OPEN: Click to open the Budget screen.
BUDGET_HINT: Every Monday the week's taxes come in and the budget is paid. A deficit comes out of the treasury; once it is empty, your country borrows. A surplus pays debt back. Debt above the credit limit means a default. The rules are Victoria 3's.
BUDGET_TREASURY_HINT: The government's money (Victoria 3's gold reserves). A deficit comes out of it; once it is empty, the country borrows.
BUDGET_BALANCE_HINT: Last week's income less last week's spending.
BUDGET_DEBT_HINT: What the government owes. It starts at your country's real 2025 debt (IMF) and grows whenever the treasury is empty and the week ends in a deficit.
BUDGET_CREDIT_HINT: How much the country can owe: its starting debt plus half a year's GDP. Interest rises from 70 % of it; above it the country defaults.
BUDGET_RATING_HINT: From AAA (little of the credit limit used) to CCC (close to it); D after a default, while the country can't borrow.
BUDGET_INTEREST_HINT: Paid every week on the debt: the country's real rate, more near the credit limit, with high inflation, and for five years after a default.
BUDGET_INFLATION_HINT: Starts at your country's real 2025 rate and settles toward 2.5 % by itself; printing money pushes it up. Prices in the game stay in 2025 dollars, so inflation shows as people's money buying less (above 10 %) and dearer borrowing.
BUDGET_GDP_HINT: The size of the economy a year; it moves with what your people earn. In brackets: the real 2025 revenue and spending as shares of GDP, where the budget started.
BUDGET_CUT_HINT: After a default the country can't borrow for two years: it pays only what comes in, and every spending line is cut to fit.
BUDGET_SETTING_TAXES_HINT: Victoria 3's tax level: multiplies every tax (income tax by stratum, dividends tax, consumption tax) and the other revenue. Higher taxes leave people less to spend, so their wealth and standard of living fall.
BUDGET_SETTING_ADMINISTRATION_HINT: The officials' wages (Victoria 3's government wages). Less funding pays them less and collects less tax.
BUDGET_SETTING_MILITARY_HINT: The soldiers' wages (Victoria 3's military wages). Upkeep and weapons come with military production (F14) and conscription (F15).
BUDGET_SETTING_WELFARE_HINT: Unemployment benefits: the unemployed get none, 10, 25, 40 or 60 % of the going wage.
BUDGET_SETTING_EDUCATION_HINT: Speeds up training for better jobs (laborers to skilled workers, skilled workers to professionals): ×0.5 to ×1.5.
BUDGET_PRINTING_HINT: An emergency option: money into the treasury every week (1, 5 or 15 % of GDP a year), but inflation rises.
BUDGET_AUTOMATIC_HINT: Let your country run its budget like the other countries do: taxes up or spending down when debt nears the limit or the deficit is big, back when it is comfortable.
BUDGET_OF_GDP_HINT: A year of this line as a share of the country's GDP.
BUDGET_LINE_INCOME_TAX_HINT: A share of every worker's wages, by stratum (laborers and soldiers the least, owners the most). Subsistence farmers pay none.
BUDGET_LINE_DIVIDENDS_TAX_HINT: A share of the dividends buildings pay their owners.
BUDGET_LINE_CONSUMPTION_TAX_HINT: Added to the price of the goods people buy, like a sales tax.
BUDGET_LINE_OTHER_REVENUE_HINT: A stand-in for everything the pops don't pay yet (corporate taxes, oil and gas money): so that your country starts with its real revenue. It grows with the economy and follows the tax level.
BUDGET_LINE_PRINTED_MONEY_HINT: Money the government prints (an emergency option that raises inflation).
BUDGET_LINE_EDUCATION_HINT: Schools and universities: they speed up training for better jobs.
BUDGET_LINE_INTEREST_HINT: Paid on the debt every week.
BUDGET_LINE_OTHER_SPENDING_HINT: A stand-in for everything the government pays for that the game doesn't have yet (health, pensions, roads, police): so that your country starts with its real spending. It grows with the economy; later features take their share out of it.
BUDGET_LINE_RESEARCH_HINT: State research (turns money into research points).
BUDGET_LINE_INFRASTRUCTURE_HINT: Roads, rail and power lines: supply and evacuation.
BUDGET_LINE_INTELLIGENCE_HINT: Intelligence networks abroad and counter-intelligence at home.
BUDGET_LINE_SUBSIDIES_HINT: Support for chosen sectors or businesses.
BUDGET_INCOME_TAX_HINT: The share of wages this group pays (by its stratum, the tax level, how well taxes are collected and the administration's funding).
BUDGET_GROSS_HINT: What a worker of this group earns today before taxes (wages, dividends), US$ a day.
BUDGET_NET_HINT: What is left after income and dividends taxes, plus unemployment benefits, US$ a day. The consumption tax then makes their goods dearer.
BUDGET_OTHER_TAXES: Dividends tax {dividends}; consumption tax {consumption}; the unemployed get {benefit} of the going wage.
BUDGET_NOTE: Every country starts with its real 2025 revenue, spending, debt, inflation and interest rate (IMF). Other countries run their budgets by themselves. Research, infrastructure and the other greyed-out lines come with their features; until then their money is part of "other spending". Taxes and unemployment will also move stability (F10) and politics.
BUDGET_TEST_CRISIS_HINT: Puts your country's debt at its credit limit with an empty treasury: its next deficit makes it default, so you can see what happens.
ALERT_BORROWING_TEXT: The treasury is empty and the budget is in deficit ({balance} a week): your country borrows. {used} of its credit limit is used.
ALERT_NEAR_LIMIT_TEXT: {used} of the credit limit is used (debt {debt}; interest {interest}). Above it your country defaults: raise taxes or cut spending.
ALERT_DEFAULT_TEXT: Your country defaulted and can't borrow: it pays only {cut} of its spending.
ALERT_INFLATION_TEXT: Inflation is {inflation} a year: people's money buys less, and borrowing costs more.
MESSAGE_DEFAULT: {country} can't pay its debts: half of them are written off, and it can't borrow for two years.
MESSAGE_DEFAULT_OWN: {country} can't pay its debts: half of them are written off, but it can't borrow for two years and must cut its spending to what comes in. Its people lose standard of living.
